title: VPC change ops checklist and audit scenarios
summary: Working draft: operator checklist for customer-managed VPC changes, with concrete audit-event schema suggestions, automated approval gates, and representative incident scenarios for private deployments. Intended for product, infra, and security review before formal PRD.
content:
Purpose
---
This doc is a practical operator-facing checklist and scenario bank for handling customer VPC/network changes in Redwood Private deployments. Focus: define minimal approval gates, what gets logged (and how), and clear runbooks for common audit/incident scenarios.

Audience
- Platform/product engineers owning private onboarding and networking handovers
- Solutions/SEs who coordinate customer network changes
- Security and compliance reviewers who evaluate audit trails and tamper-evidence

Background/context (quick)
- Customers run Redwood Private behind customer-managed VPCs or on-prem networks. Changes to routing, peering, firewall rules, and NAT/Gateway settings can materially affect availability and data paths.
- We need clear operator steps + machine-readable audit events so customers + Redwood can investigate incidents and prove change lineage for compliance.

Goals
1) Standardize a lightweight approval flow that prevents accidental production-impacting network changes without blocking legitimate operator work.
2) Ensure every change is recorded in an append-only audit stream with immutable metadata (actor, ticket, diff, signed fingerprint) and retention policy.
3) Provide concrete runbooks for rollback, escalation, and post-incident reporting.

Constraints and guiding principles
- Minimal latency: approval gates should use async ticket/PR model (canary/testing in isolated control plane before full rollout).
- Customer control: any automated tooling must respect customer-managed controls (no backdoor changes to customer VPC).
- Audit integrity: prefer cryptographic signing (HMAC or KMS-based signatures) for Redwood-originated audit entries.

Roles and responsibilities (proposed)
- Network Operator (customer or Redwood-assigned): initiates the change, provides diff + justification, attaches test plan.
- Reviewer (Redwood network/security engineer): verifies policy compliance, escalation if risk high.
- Approver (product owner or customer security admin): final gate.
- On-call SRE: monitors health post-change and owns rollback if metrics degrade.

Approval gate flow (lightweight)
1) Create ticket (Jira/Linear) containing: change diff, expected outage window (if any), verification steps, rollback steps, linked customer change request. Ticket must use template with structured fields.
2) Automated preflight checks run: syntax lint of terraform/cli diff, conflict detection with scheduled changes, collisions with reserved ports. Preflight results attached to ticket.
3) Reviewer approval required for any change that alters: route tables, network ACLs, managed firewall rules, peering/Transit Gateway attachments. Minor metadata updates (tags) can be auto-approved.
4) Approval recorded as an audit event containing: ticket id, approver id, time, decision metadata, signed-hash of change payload.
5) Change executed in canary (if available) -> health checks -> full rollout. All phases produce audit events.

Audit event schema (suggested fields; machine-friendly event lines in a streaming audit log)
- event_id: UUID
- timestamp: ISO8601
- event_type: CHANGE_REQUEST | APPROVAL | EXECUTE_STEP | ROLLBACK | HEALTH_CHECK
- actor: user:email or service:role
- ticket_id: JIRA/LINEAR id
- change_summary: short string
- change_diff: base64-or-escaped-diff (store small; pointer to artifact if large)
- target_scope: vpc-id / subnet / route-table / firewall-id
- phase: preflight|canary|rollout|complete|rollback
- result: success|failure|warning
- signature: base64(HMAC(KMS_key_id, concat(event_id,timestamp,actor,ticket_id)))
- provenance: [artifact_urls] (list)

Notes on retention and storage
- Write all events to customer-dedicated audit-bucket (or customer-managed syslog endpoint). Default retention 90 days; enterprise option 1 year+ (configurable per contract).
- Append-only log with immutable sequence numbers. Redwood stores signed copies; if customer opts for push-to-customer-syslog, Redwood still retains signed digest (small) to validate later.

Tamper-evidence and signing
- Option A (recommended): Redwood signs each event with a KMS key; store signature + key id in event. Use SHA256 HMAC with KMS-managed symmetric key for speed.
- Option B: For highest assurance, store event hashes in an external timestamping service (e.g., public ledger or a third-party attestation service) — heavy-weight, opt-in for customers who need it.

Concrete checklist for operator before change (quick actionable)
- [ ] Ticket created with required template (ticket id present in commit message).
- [ ] Preflight checks passed (attach logs).
- [ ] Peer review / Security review status recorded in ticket.
- [ ] Approver signoff recorded (audit event generated).
- [ ] Canary environment exists and smoke tests defined.
- [ ] Rollback procedure documented (exact terraform plan or CLI commands).
- [ ] KMS signing enabled for this customer (if contract requires).
- [ ] Monitoring alerts configured (latency, 5xx rates, pod restarts, egress errors).
- [ ] Post-change verification checklist attached to ticket.

Representative incident scenarios (for runbook testing)
1) Scenario: Route table change removes path to cache layer -> increased latency, error ramp
   - Detection: spike in 5xx and SLO violation alert, synthetic checks fail
   - Immediate actions: mark change as in-progress in ticket; initiate rollback command; contact on-call SRE
   - Audit needs: event sequence from APPROVAL -> EXECUTE_STEP -> HEALTH_CHECK -> ROLLBACK with signatures and timestamps
\2) Scenario: Mis-applied security group rule opens wide egress -> potential data exfil risk
   - Detection: netflow anomaly; IDS alert; customer reports suspicious traffic
   - Immediate actions: disable rule, move affected instances to isolated subnet, rotate keys if egress to unknown host observed
   - Postmortem: need packet-level flow logs + audit trail proving who applied the change
\3) Scenario: Peering attach succeeded but BGP routes not announced -> partial failure
   - Detection: traffic blackholing for a subset of services
   - Actions: validate BGP session status, re-run canary, re-apply correct ASN mapping, escalate networking SME

Queries and example investigator workflows
- Quickly find all changes by operator X in last 30 days: SELECT * FROM audit_stream WHERE actor = 'user:ashap@redwood.ai' AND event_type = 'EXECUTE_STEP' AND timestamp > :30d
- Validate change integrity: retrieve event by id, verify signature using KMS key id, compare change_diff artifact hash
- Reconstruct timeline for postmortem: pull all events with ticket_id = JIRA-3141 and sort by timestamp

Runbook snippets (rollback)
- If canary fails: run terraform apply -target=module.network.canary_rollback --auto-approve; emit ROLLBACK audit event with cause and operator id
- If full rollback required: consult ticket rollback steps; use signed command token flow (operator signs rollback with their key; system validates and requires second approver for cross-account rollbacks)

Metrics to surface in Console (minimum)
- Avg time from ticket creation -> approval
- Fraction of changes that require rollback
- Audit ingestion lag (time between event generation -> available in search)
- Signature verification success rate

Open questions / tradeoffs (to resolve in PRD)
- Should we require 2-step approval for all peering/route-table changes or only for cross-account changes? (security vs friction)
- Storage: default 90d for hosted logs, but many enterprise customers want longer retention; pricing model?
- Signature model: symmetric KMS HMAC is fast but relies on Redwood KMS; some customers may demand customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS). Need to design key-authority flow and key rotation UX.

Next steps (short)
- Product to decide approval-level policy matrix for change classes (due: 2025-11-20)
- Infra to prototype audit-event HMAC signing and store a signed digest per ticket (owner: Miguel R., target: 2025-11-30)
- Security to review tamper-evidence proposal and map to compliance controls (SOC2/ISO) (owner: Jordan K.)
- Build minimal Console surface for ticket -> audit-event linking (PO: Asha P.)

Notes / loose thoughts (scratch)
- Could integrate with customer SIEM via syslog; need to keep mapping table of event fields to common CEF/JSON formats
- Consider a small signed digest file per day per customer to reduce query costs while keeping integrity
- We should publish an operator cheat-sheet (1-pager) for SEs and customers during handover
